title: Merged litter: 8x less hung up, but still not on the floor
question: You said the vast majority should land on the ground, and that sending it all there was fine. It is much better than it was -- 8x fewer cells hung up on branches -- but only 30% is within three rows of the ground; the rest sits in a band up in the lower crown. Is that good enough, or should a shed leaf go all the way down every time?
context_md:
Cyan = litter resting on the ground. Magenta = litter resting on a branch. 8 trees, 12,000 frames, world 512x320, ground at row 200.

Before this merge the same scene stood at **4,330 litter cells, 3,825 of them on plant tissue (88%)**. The shed leaf is now walked down through its own crown instead of being written where it hung.
